title: Failure Mode Matrix & TraceLinker: correlated error taxonomy and dashboards
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Goal: Define and instrument a deterministic Failure Mode Matrix (FMM) across Redwood services and ship the TraceLinker pipeline + dashboard surface that lets on-call and SRE correlate traces, log events, and model-level errors. This ticket covers taxonomy design, OpenTelemetry trace hooks, log/metric routing rules (Vector->Kinesis->Data Warehouse), dashboard wireframes, and a rollout plan with safety gates.

Scope and non-goals:
- In scope: failure taxonomy (timeouts, overload/backpressure, model decoding errors, tokenization errors, KV cache corruption, upstream 5xx/gRPC status codes, auth/permission failures, rate-limits), instrumentation points for request/response lifecycle, a set of aggregations and tags for the FMM, a TraceLinker microservice that enriches traces with failure labels and model diagnostics, and three dashboard views (Service Summary, Failure Heatmap, Trace Drilldown).
- Out of scope: full downstream root-cause automation (separate RFC), long-term storage changes beyond current retention, and enterprise-only RBAC on dashboards (handled by console RBAC roadmap).

Why this work: Current paging incidents require manual correlation across logs, jaeger traces, and model outputs. We need a repeatable classification so we can: (1) track error budgets per failure mode, (2) create targeted alerts and runbooks, and (3) measure regressions after model or runtime changes.

Instrumentation plan (high level):
1) Add OpenTelemetry semantic attributes at entry/egress points: request.id, route, model.variant, seq.len, kv.cache.hit, batch.size.
2) Create an error classification function in the runtime that emits a standardized error_code and error_category (see taxonomy below) to the span and to structured logs.
3) TraceLinker service subscribes to processed traces (Tempo/OTLP), correlates with structured logs (Vector pipeline), and labels trace top-level span with failure categories and top-N contributing spans.
4) Metrics pipeline: derive failure counts by category + latency histograms (p50/p95/p99) and ship to Prometheus/Signal (existing metrics infra).

Failure taxonomy (proposed canonical names):
- TIMEOUT_EXTERNAL: Upstream service/gateway timeout (HTTP/gRPC deadlines exceeded).
- TIMEOUT_MODEL: Model decode/generation exceeded configured token deadline.
- OVERLOAD_QUEUE: Request rejected by local queue/backpressure (circuit, rate-limit, quota).
- OVERLOAD_RESOURCE: OOM, CUDA OOM, or GPU memory pressure causing evictions.
- MODEL_DECODING: Tokenization/decoding mismatch, invalid tokens, bad sampling responses.
- MODEL_RUNTIME: Model runtime exceptions (nan, numerical instability, KV cache corruption).
- NETWORK_5XX: Upstream 5xx or gRPC UNAVAILABLE when not a pure timeout.
- AUTH_DENIED: SSO/SAML/KMS failures or signed request auth failures.
- CLIENT_ERROR: 4xx client issues that map to malformed requests or schema validation.
- RATE_LIMITED: Per-token or per-route rate limiting enforced.
- CACHE_STALE: KV cache or prefix cache inconsistency causing stale results (heuristic).
- CONFIG_MISMATCH: Rollout/config mismatch between control plane and runtime (e.g., pinned model missing).

Dashboard surface requirements (acceptance criteria):
- Service Summary: top-level heatmap with failure categories (rows) x routes/models (columns), sortable by error rate or impact (estimated cost).
- Failure Heatmap: time-series stacked by category with p50/p95 latency overlays and capacity signals (GPU util).
- Trace Drilldown: single-click from a heatmap cell opens a linked TraceView with highlighted spans that contributed to classification and a list of correlated log entries.
- Filters: by customer-id, environment (prod/staging), model.variant, region, and time-window.
- Export: Ability to export daily failure counts by category and route to CSV for postmortems.

Success criteria (quantitative):
- Reduce mean MTTR for incidents attributed to model/runtime errors by 35% within 2 quarters.
- 90% of incidents show a primary failure category assigned by TraceLinker within 60s of first error.
- Dashboards show meaningful signal (top 5 routes) and are used by at least 3 on-call engineers in the first week after rollout (measured via dashboard usages).

Rollout phases and timeline:
- Phase 0 (2 weeks): Finalize taxonomy, wireframes, and proto attributes.
- Phase 1 (3 weeks): Add runtime span attrs + structured logging changes; deploy TraceLinker prototype in dev.
- Phase 2 (2 weeks): Metrics pipeline and dashboard alpha; limited prod sampling on low-traffic accounts.
- Phase 3 (2 weeks): Full prod rollout + on-call training and runbooks.

Risks & mitigations:
- False positives in classification -> add confidence score to spans and build operator to tune rules.
- Additional cardinality in traces -> limit high-cardinality attributes and rely on enriched logs for bulk info.
- Privacy/customer data in traces -> ensure PII redaction at instrument points and enforce retention.

Notes: links to RFCs and artifacts in attachments.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Taxonomy doc published and approved by SRE+Runtime by 2026-02-14. 2) TraceLinker prototype returns error_category tag on 95% of sampled failing traces in dev. 3) Dashboards alpha accepted by on-call squad with at least two drilldown examples. 4) Runbook templates added to Confluence and linked in dashboard.
comments: 2026-02-11 | Ava Chen: Kickoff meeting summary: agreed to canonicalize names and keep taxonomy flat (no nested hierarchies). Diego to own TraceLinker service. Action items: taxonomy draft due 2026-02-13, wireframes by 2026-02-16.

2026-02-14 | Diego Morales: Taxonomy v0 published: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Failure+Mode+Matrix+v0. Added initial mapping for HTTP 408->TIMEOUT_EXTERNAL, gRPC DEADLINE_EXCEEDED->TIMEOUT_EXTERNAL, gRPC RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED->OVERLOAD_RESOURCE. Need runtime review from @Sana Gupta on model-level error signaling.

2026-02-17 | Sana Gupta: Reviewed taxonomy. Feedback: separate MODEL_DECODING from MODEL_RUNTIME — decoding errors are almost always client input. Also requested span attribute model.quantization_level. Filing follow-up ENG-47222 for model attr additions.

2026-02-19 | Diego Morales: Prototype TraceLinker deployed to dev; it consumes traces from our Tempo consumer and enriches top-level spans with error_category and confidence. Found noisy client_error classification when request.schema validation emits multiple errors; added dedupe logic. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/tracelinker/pull/12

2026-02-23 | QA (Liam O'Neill): Alpha dashboard available at https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/obs/fmm-alpha. Found mismatch between log timestamps and span timestamps for ~2% traces — filed ENG-47223 to normalize timestamp ingestion. Also flagged that p99 latency appears undercounted for long-polling routes.

2026-02-27 | PM (Nora Patel): Reviewed rollout plan and customer impact. Recommend canary on Dedicated customers only for first week. Approved release gating criteria. Added runbook templates to Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Runbooks+for+FMM
